sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring A Little Shameless. You know what you want to say, but another demand arrives first: make sure nobody sees you struggle. You postpone the question, soften your opinion or wait for a safer moment that never arrives.

In this session, we will recognise the wish to hide, separate permission from rudeness, and try a respectful small request. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: A little shameless is permission to be seen while you are still learning. Here it means that an imperfect word does not have to be hidden before you can participate. It does not ask you to be rude, ignore the listener or perform boldness. A shy person may need a stronger phrase because be confident has become one more difficult instruction. We will use the phrase only if it helps you move.

sections.narration:
You know what you want to say, but another demand arrives first: make sure nobody sees you struggle. You postpone the question, soften your opinion or wait for a safer moment that never arrives.

Embarrassment is a feeling, and concealment is an action you may take around it. You may not choose whether embarrassment appears today. You can experiment with whether it chooses every action afterwards. A small visible contribution is enough. You do not need to make a dramatic disclosure, deliberately stammer in public or seek a difficult audience.

sections.narration: If shameless feels unkind or artificial, use willing to be seen. The phrase is a handle, not a new identity. Feeling embarrassed afterwards does not erase the contribution you made. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: Try one low-pressure request that you have been delaying. Afterwards write: I allowed myself to __. Leave out a score for bravery. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
